name: Stannous sulfate
description: Stannous sulfate (CAS 7488-55-3 ), also known as tin(II) sulfate, is an inorganic tin salt used primarily as a source of stannous ions in electroplating baths and surface finishing processes. It functions as a catalyst and surface modification agent across electronics manufacturing, textile processing, and specialty chemical applications. In electronics and printed circuit board manufacturing, it is a key electrolyte component. The product is used in acid tin plating baths, depositing uniform tin coatings on copper substrates for solderability and corrosion resistance. Textile and leather processors use it as a mordant and reducing agent. These applications help to fix dyes and improve color fastness on natural fibers. In the printing and packaging sector, it supports tin-based electrodeposition on metal substrates used in food-grade packaging production. It also serves as a catalyst precursor in polymer synthesis and certain organic esterification reactions where controlled stannous ion activity is required. The material is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity levels typically ranging from 95% to 99%+. High-purity grades are available for electronics and plating applications where strict tin content is necessary. These specialized grades ensure low heavy metal impurity specifications are met for sensitive industrial processes.
